source.title: Information bottleneck theory of high-dimensional regression: relevancy, efficiency and optimality

record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and reports information-theoretic analogs of sample-wise double and multiple descent, but does not measure test error or test any of the listed versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The paper reports residual-information and information-efficiency behavior, not test error. Those information-theoretic results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Results about double descent cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper measures residual information I(T;Y|W) and information efficiency in Gaussian linear regression, not test error or risk. It calls the nonmonotonicity an 'information-theoretic analog' of double descent. The authors say the link to test-error double descent 'remains to be seen', and no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors derive information-theoretic analogs of double and multiple descent in residual information. Because residual information bounds the generalization gap, they think it may connect to test-error double descent, but they leave the depth of that connection open.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes Gaussian linear regression using information-theoretic quantities and random-matrix results, rather than sweeping deep-network size, training epochs, or sample size while measuring test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Under anisotropic covariates, the number and locations of residual-information maxima change; the first maximum shifts with anisotropy. Gibbs-regression information efficiency also depends on regularization strength and sample ratio.

fits_no_version.finding:
Isotropic covariates: residual information of the IB optimal algorithm and of Gibbs regression (λ=10^-6) grows linearly with N for N

P, peaking near N/P≈1 (Fig 2e).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In high-dimensional linear regression, residual (overfitting) information peaks near the interpolation crossover N≈P as sample size varies.

fits_no_version.finding: Two-scale anisotropic covariates: a second residual-information maximum appears at larger N/P, attributed to low-variance directions. For the optimal algorithm, the first maximum shifts to lower N/P as anisotropy increases (Fig 3d).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Covariate anisotropy produces multiple sample-wise maxima in residual information.

fits_no_version.finding: The information efficiency of Gibbs regression relative to the IB optimum approaches 1 as N/P→0 and as N/P→∞, and is lowest near N/P=1 (Fig 2d, Fig 4c). Under anisotropy, efficiency depends more strongly on λ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomized ridge regression is least information-efficient near the interpolation threshold.

record.problems: The reported descent results concern residual information, not test error; the authors explicitly leave the connection to the original test-error phenomenon unresolved. The analysis is for specified linear-regression models and high-dimensional limits, not deep networks. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results relevant to the listed test-error versions were available to extract. Cited results from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: Model-wise test-error double descent in deep networks is not studied.
Epoch-wise double descent is not studied.
Test error versus sample size is not computed; only residual information is.
Risk curves across model classes or capacity are not reported.
No effective-complexity measure predicting the location of a test-error peak.
Noise, multiple-peak and regularization effects are analysed only for residual information and efficiency, not test error.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given, because no row measures test error or risk. The efficiency-minimum result is added under fits_no_version with no row; consider adding a row for it from Fig 2d and Fig 4c.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test-error double descent in deep networks.
Whether increasing training sample size near the interpolation threshold raises test error.
Risk curves across model classes and capacity.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes.
Whether test-error peaks are driven by label noise or variance, split into multiple peaks, or disappear under optimally tuned regularization.
Whether counting effective parameters turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: IB optimal algorithm
rows.operation_detail: Analyze residual information as sample size changes in the high-dimensional limit.
rows.value: Nonmonotonic in sample size: extensive for N/P < 1 and decreases in the data-abundant regime; the paper describes a maximum around the under- to overparametrized crossover.
rows.note: This is an information-theoretic analog, not a test-error measurement.

rows.subject: Gibbs regression
rows.operation_detail: Analyze residual information as sample size changes.
rows.value: Nonmonotonic in sample size: it grows linearly with N when N/P < 1 and decreases as sample size exceeds P; the paper describes a maximum around the crossover.
rows.note: The paper presents this as an information-theoretic analog of double descent, not as test error.
